messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition (ΔV ≈ –8.98 × 10⁻⁵ m³ kg⁻¹, ΔH ≈ 333.5 kJ kg⁻¹, T ≈ 273 K) gives:

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}\;=\;\frac{T\,\Delta V}{\Delta H}\;\approx\;-7.4\times10^{-5}\ \text{K Pa}^{-1}
\]

Multiplying by 10 kPa (10 000 Pa) yields a shift of about –0.74 K.  
Thus the freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly:

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \;\approx\; 0.0^\circ\text{C} \;-\; 0.7^\circ\text{C}
\;\approx\; -0.7^\circ\text{C}
\]

So, **the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is about –0.7 °C**.
